newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Schuessel survives no confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Schuessel survives no confidence vote.

text.p: Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel survived a no confidence vote on Friday after opposition parties said a string of alleged blunders had irrevocably damaged the country's image.
Schuessel's career was hanging by a thread after German weekly magazine Focus alleged he called Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer "a real pig" at a recent European Union summit in Amsterdam.
Schuessel, who is also leader of the conservative People's Party and Vice-Chancellor, strenuously denied the report by journalists at the summit.

Austrian media had said Schuessel's alleged outburst was triggered by a row between German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and the Bundesbank over the Bonn government's plans to revalue the central bank's gold reserves.
Schuessel, who is never without his trademark bow tie and red-rimmed glasses, flew to Frankfurt to reassure Tietmeyer of his innocence.

National media also alleged the outspoken minister called Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson an "idiot", an African foreign minister a "barefoot", U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright an "old Bette Davis" and Edith Cresson, French former prime minister and EU commissioner, an "old bag".
The vote of no-confidence was staged by Joerg Haider's far-right Freedom Party, the Greens and the Liberal Forum.

But the dominant Social Democrats of Chancellor Viktor Klima, and coalition partners the People's Party, threw their weight behind Schuessel and defeated the motion in a five-hour debate on the last day of parliament before the summer recess.
